scholarship_name: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
provider: Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst (DAAD)
applies_to_institution: Technische Universitaet Berlin|Charite - Universitaetsmedizin Berlin|Freie Universitaet Berlin|Humboldt-Universitaet zu Berlin
applies_to_programs: Urban Management - UM (MSc 18 months TU Berlin)|Master of Science in International Health (MSc 12 months Charite Berlin/FU Berlin/HU Berlin)
amount_notes: 992 EUR/month for graduates (1300 EUR/month for doctoral candidates; 1400 EUR from Feb 2026). Plus health/accident/personal-liability insurance contributions and a travel allowance unless covered elsewhere. Possible monthly rent subsidy and family allowance. Berlin public universities charge no tuition so the stipend is effectively net living money.
duration_covered: 12 to 42 months depending on the study programme (TU Berlin Urban Management = 18 months)
nationality_restrictions: Only nationals of countries on the DAAD/OECD-DAC developing-country list for EPOS
tunisia_eligible_evidence: "Graduates with at least two years' professional experience from the following countries: list of eligible countries" - the DAC list names under NORTH AFRICA: Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco, Tunesia.
other_eligibility: Bachelor (normally four-year) in a related subject; degree in the upper third of the class; AT LEAST TWO YEARS of relevant professional experience after the first degree at the time of application; degree not more than six years old; not resident in Germany >15 months at the deadline. Max 3 courses per applicant.
application_window: Set by each individual EPOS course, not by the DAAD; applications go directly to the course. Current list is 'List of all Postgraduate courses with application deadlines 2027/2028' (Stand 06/2026).
deadline: Course-specific - see the DAAD EPOS deadlines list for 2027/2028; TU Berlin Urban Management and Charite International Health both say 'see website of the course'
deadline_source_cycle: 2027/2028 cycle (DAAD EPOS deadline list Stand 06/2026)
apply_via: Directly to the chosen postgraduate course (NOT to the DAAD) using the DAAD EPOS application form + checklist
red_flags: THE TWO-YEAR PROFESSIONAL-EXPERIENCE BAR IS ABSOLUTE - a 2027 graduate straight out of the engineering diploma is NOT eligible. Only 2 Berlin courses exist and neither is software/music. German-track courses require B1 German at application and DSH-2/TestDaF-4 before the course starts.
notes: German-language proficiency IS a funding condition for German-taught EPOS courses (B1 certificate at application, DSH 2 / TestDaF 4 before study start; a 6-month German course in Germany is included). For English-taught courses only English per course rules. Both Berlin courses are English-taught. Realistic only if the client works 2+ years before applying.

scholarship_name: DAAD Study Scholarships - Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines

provider: Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst (DAAD)
applies_to_institution: any
applies_to_city: any (Germany, incl. all Berlin state universities)
amount_notes: 992 EUR/month, plus insurance contributions, travel allowance on application, annual study allowance of 460 EUR, possible rent subsidy, Green Mobility top-up, funded online language course and 2/4/6-month German course before the study visit.

nationality_restrictions: Restricted to a closed country list which is essentially Europe, the CIS, and industrialised countries

other_eligibility: First degree by the start of funding; last degree not older than 6 years; not resident in Germany >15 months at deadline.

deadline_source_cycle: 2027 cycle (funding must begin in 2027)

red_flags: CLOSED TO TUNISIANS. DAAD's own overview says master's study scholarships are 'available, in particular, for persons from industrial countries'. Do not waste an application cycle here.
notes: Logged specifically so the client does not chase it. DAAD routes developing/emerging-country applicants to EPOS and the STEM study scholarships instead - but see FBE-007: the STEM line also excludes Tunisia. scholarship_name: DAAD Study Scholarships - Music
provider: Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst (DAAD)

applies_to_programs: Master / postgraduate music degree (2nd cycle) or Konzertexamen/Meisterklasse (3rd cycle)|Advanced studies without a degree
amount_notes: 992 EUR/month, travel allowance on application, one-off study allowance, health/accident/personal-liability insurance contributions, possible rent subsidy and family allowance, Green Mobility top-up, funded online language course plus a 2/4/6-month German course before the study visit.
duration_covered: Degree studies: 2 to 4 semesters (10-24 months). Advanced studies without a degree: 12 months, extendable in individual cases.
nationality_restrictions: Open worldwide - very long country list including Tunisia
tunisia_eligible_evidence: Country selector for this programme includes "...Trinidad and Tobago Tunisia Turkey Turkmenistan Uganda Ukraine..."; DAAD: "Please select your status and your country to enable you to submit an application".
other_eligibility: "you will have obtained a first degree in music by the time the scholarship begins, or you have exhausted all training opportunities for your instrument or subject in your home country if no degree is offered in your country of origin". Last degree <=6 years old; not resident in Germany >15 months. Funds only ARTISTIC projects - musicology/music education/scientific projects are excluded.
application_window: Applications via the DAAD portal; portal opens 1 June and closes on the deadline below
deadline: 24 September 2026 (Bewerbungsschluss 24.09.2026); selection meeting February 2027; funding starts from October 2027
deadline_source_cycle: 2027 cycle - this IS the window for a September/October 2027 start
apply_via: DAAD portal (portal.daad.de) + artistic work samples via the DAAD media database
red_flags: HARD BLOCKER FOR THIS CLIENT: requires a FIRST DEGREE IN MUSIC (or proof that no music degree exists in the home country and all local training has been exhausted). A software-engineering diploma plus a portfolio does not satisfy this. Audition/work-sample gated. Deadline 24 Sept 2026 is roughly one month away.
notes: German is NOT a funding condition per se - DAAD asks only for 'sufficient knowledge of the language of instruction' by the start of the scholarship; a German course is funded if needed and is compulsory only where the course is taught in German. Berlin's state music schools (UdK Berlin, HfM Hanns Eisler) teach mostly in German, which would make German a de-facto condition there.

applies_to_programs: DAAD-selected English-taught master's courses in Social and Political Sciences, Law, Economics, Public Policy and Administration
amount_notes: 992 EUR/month, health insurance in Germany, lump-sum travel allowances, a study and research grant, rent subsidies and family supplements as applicable. application_window: 1 June to 31 July 2026 for the September/October 2027 intake - THIS WINDOW HAS ALREADY CLOSED
deadline_source_cycle: 2027 cycle (official call ST42 Helmut-Schmidt-Programm - Stipendienausschreibung 05/2026) - CLOSED; 2028 cycle expected to open 1 June 2027

scholarship_name: COST BASELINE - Semesterbeitrag and tuition at Berlin public universities (not a scholarship)
provider: Land Berlin state universities (TU Berlin, FU Berlin, HTW Berlin, HWR Berlin, BHT Berlin)
applies_to_institution: Technische Universitaet Berlin|Freie Universitaet Berlin|Hochschule fuer Technik und Wirtschaft Berlin (HTW)|Hochschule fuer Wirtschaft und Recht Berlin (HWR)|Berliner Hochschule fuer Technik (BHT)
amount_notes: Semester fee WINTER SEMESTER 2026/27, per semester, official figures: TU Berlin 379.06 EUR (admin 50.00 + student body 14.56 + studierendenWERK 85.00 + Semesterticket 226.80 + ticket social fund 2.70; 149.56 without the ticket). HWR Berlin 379.77 EUR (50.00 + 85.00 + AStA 17.97 + 226.80; 152.97 without ticket). FU Berlin 376.80 EUR (studierendenWERK 85.00 + admin 50.00 + AStA 10.00 + Deutschlandsemesterticket 226.80 + social fund 5.00). BHT Berlin 376.30 EUR (50.00 + 85.00 + student body 11.50 + ticket 226.80 + social fund 3.00). HTW Berlin 375.30 EUR (exchange students 325.30 EUR). Late re-registration surcharge 19.94 EUR everywhere.
duration_covered: Per semester, payable at enrolment and at every re-registration
nationality_restrictions: None - the same fee applies to EU and non-EU students
tunisia_eligible_evidence: HWR Berlin: "Studierende im Land Berlin zahlen derzeit fuer Bachelor- und konsekutive Masterstudiengaenge keine Studiengebuehren an den staatlichen Hochschulen." FU Berlin: "Die Freie Universitaet Berlin erhebt - ausser fuer weiterbildende Studienangebote - keine Studiengebuehren."
other_eligibility: The Semesterticket component (226.80 EUR) buys the Deutschlandsemesterticket - unlimited local and regional public transport across Germany for the whole semester. It is compulsory for on-campus students; exemption/subsidy schemes exist via the AStA social fund.
application_window: Payable by the enrolment / re-registration deadline each semester
deadline: Re-registration deadline each semester (TU Berlin: last Friday of lecture period at FU Berlin)
deadline_source_cycle: Winter semester 2026/27 figures - 2027/28 figures TBC but historically move by only a few euros
apply_via: Bank transfer to the university cashier
red_flags: NO TUITION applies only to Bachelor and CONSECUTIVE master's programmes at STATE universities. Weiterbildende (continuing-education / non-consecutive / executive) master's DO charge real fees even at state universities - HTW's Division of Continuing Education pays a different fee, and FU explicitly excludes weiterbildende Studienangebote from the no-tuition rule. Private Berlin institutions charge full tuition.
notes: This row exists so the Wave 4 ranking has the true Berlin cost in one place. Non-EU status changes NOTHING about the fee. Effective annual cost of studying at a Berlin public university = roughly 750-760 EUR of semester fees plus living costs; the semester fee already includes a Germany-wide transport ticket worth far more than its price. HU Berlin and UdK Berlin figures could not be retrieved (HU is behind an anti-bot wall, UdK has no published fee page found) - TBC, but the 50 EUR admin + 85 EUR studierendenWERK + 226.80 EUR ticket components are set by Land Berlin regulation and are identical everywhere.

scholarship_name: VISA COST BASELINE - German student visa proof of funds (Sperrkonto) for Tunisian applicants
scholarship_name_original: Finanzierungsnachweis / Sperrkonto - Check-list Etudes, Ambassade d'Allemagne Tunis
provider: Auswaertiges Amt / German Embassy Tunis (Ambassade d'Allemagne a Tunis)
applies_to_institution: any
amount_notes: German Embassy Tunis study-visa checklist: the amount required to finance one year of study is 11,904 EUR (992 EUR per month). Accepted proof: (a) a blocked account IN GERMANY, or (b) a Verpflichtungserklaerung under ss.66-68 AufenthG by a person resident in Germany. Since February 2023 the Embassy accepts ONLY a blocked account held at a GERMAN bank - a Tunisian blocked account is no longer accepted. National visa (D) fee 75.00 EUR, payable in TND in cash.
duration_covered: One year (renewed for each subsequent year via the Auslaenderbehoerde)
nationality_restrictions: Applies to Tunisian nationals applying at the Embassy in Tunis
tunisia_eligible_evidence: "Le montant prevu pour le financement d'une annee d'etudes s'eleve a 11.904 EUR (992 EUR par mois) (a) compte bloque en Allemagne" - Check-list Etudes, Ambassade d'Allemagne Tunis.
other_eligibility: The Etudes checklist also demands an UNCONDITIONAL admission letter (Certificat d'admission inconditionnel) plus proof of language: DSH or TestDaF for German-taught programmes, IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent for English-taught ones; a legalised baccalaureat and legalised university diploma with transcripts; and proof of health insurance.
application_window: Waiting-list registration with the Embassy, then an appointment via TLScontact; studies/study-preparation visas can now also be filed through the Consular Services Portal
deadline: No fixed deadline - but processing can take up to three months and appointment waiting times are published per category
deadline_source_cycle: Current as displayed 2026-08-22 (Etudes checklist page dated 25.07.2024; visa overview page updated 29.06.2026)
apply_via: German Embassy Tunis / TLScontact / Consular Services Portal (VIDEX form)
red_flags: 11,904 EUR must be liquid and parked in a GERMAN blocked account before the visa interview - this is the single largest cash barrier in the Berlin plan, and it is roughly 16x the annual semester fee. It changes yearly with the BAfoeG maximum rate; re-check in spring 2027.
notes: A SCHOLARSHIP REMOVES THIS REQUIREMENT. The Embassy runs a separate checklist, 'Boursiers d'Etat allemand/Erasmus+' (Boursiers d'Etat allemand / Erasmus+), whose document list contains NO financing proof at all - only the scholarship award letter (attestation de bourse), the German university's confirmation, passport, photos and health insurance for the whole stay. Scholarship holders also skip the waiting list (they book directly with TLScontact) and the 75 EUR visa fee is waived for holders of publicly funded scholarships. That makes 'win a public scholarship' worth about 12,000 EUR of liquidity on top of the stipend itself.

scholarship_name: Avicenna-Studienwerk International Scholarship Programme (ISP)

NOT fundable: Bildungsinlaender, bachelor's, part-time study, Staatsexamen, a second master's, and double funding by another Begabtenfoerderungswerk. Documents: motivation letter (max 2pp), CV (max 2pp), school-leaving certificate, university and work certificates, enrolment certificate if available, proof of social engagement, two academic references, passport copy, transcript of records.
application_window: 1 March to 15 April 2026 for funding starting 1 October 2026 - so expect roughly 1 March to 15 April 2027 for a 1 October 2027 start
deadline_source_cycle: 2026 cycle - 2027 TBC (window pattern 01.03.-15.04. for a 1 October funding start)
apply_via: Avicenna online application portal (currently closed)
red_flags: The programme is explicitly for MUSLIM students - a confessional criterion the client must be comfortable declaring. No published country list, so Tunisia is 'likely' rather than confirmed; a one-line email to Enes Erdogan at Avicenna would settle it. Enrolment certificate must be supplied as soon as it exists.
notes: STRONGEST NON-DAAD PRE-ARRIVAL ROUTE FOUND FOR THIS CLIENT. No German-language condition is stated anywhere in the ISP call - documents may be submitted in German OR English, unlike the regular Avicenna Studienfoerderung which demands C1/DSH-2 from non-EU applicants. All subjects are eligible, so a computer-science or media/sound master's in Berlin fits. 1,044 EUR/month exceeds the DAAD rate. The application window (March-April 2027) sits AFTER most Berlin master's application deadlines, which is convenient: admission first, scholarship second.

scholarship_name: Heinrich-Boell-Stiftung Studienwerk - scholarship for international students (Bildungsauslaender)

notes: Tunisia's DAC status is an ADVANTAGE here, not a barrier - Boell gives priority to DAC-country applicants who are still at home when they apply, which is exactly the client's situation in early 2027. Application forms and the expert-report form exist in English (A1-1b, A1-3b, A1-4b), which strongly suggests German is not a hard funding condition - but this is not stated explicitly, so treat the German requirement as TBC.

Worth an email to KAS asking whether Tunisian applicants can use the in-Germany route or a neighbouring office.

Grades obtained abroad must be officially converted into the German grading system (e.g. a uni-assist Vorpruefungsdokumentation); self-conversions are not accepted. Not for doctoral students.

UdK Berlin: "Am 1. Oktober 2026 werden voraussichtlich neue Stipendien an dieser Stelle ausgeschrieben."

This is the single most accessible Berlin scheme for a non-EU student because nationality is irrelevant and admission is not required first. Best used as a stackable supplement; note that it cannot be combined with a Studienstiftung or other BMFTR Begabtenfoerderungswerk scholarship, and Rosa-Luxemburg explicitly excludes double funding with it.
